title: Nasdaq is down for the year after Anthropic IPO doesn't soothe AI jitters
byline: Huileng Tan, Theron Mohamed, Jennifer Sor
excerpt: Anthropic stock dropped sharply alongside a deeper sell-off across tech. The Nasdaq Composite fell slightly into the red for 2026.
content_html:
Red Friday: S&P 500 and the Dow hit correction territory, Nasdaq turns negative for the year

By Huileng Tan

2026-11-20T19:04:57.804Z

The biggest IPO in history couldn't stop the bleeding in the broader market.

US tech shares fell sharply on Friday, with the Nasdaq Composite dropping nearly 3% to turn slightly negative for 2026. The S&P 500 was headed for a seventh-straight down day, on track for the worst losing streak since 2020. The benchmark index entered an official correction, down 10% from the October 6 peak, while the Dow also entered an official correction in late afternoon trading.

Here's where major indexes stood at 2 p.m. ET:

  • S&P 500: 7,027.22, down 2%
  • Dow Jones Industrial Average: 48,826.87, down 0.55% (-270 points)
  • Nasdaq 100: 25,515.80, down 3.8%

Anthropic stock fell 12% $85 a share after surging 17% in its debut on Thursday. Other tech heavyweights were also in the red, with SpaceX and Nvidia both down 6%, Meta falling 3%, and AMD stock down another 10% after its 8% fall on Thursday sparked by a short-seller's report about its exposure to China.

Nvidia's slide is particularly stark. The AI chip titan has lost 44% of its value since its October high of $243.37 as investors continue to flee the stock after Jensen Huang's departure and following its latest earnings.

Selling in stocks helped the bond market catch a bid on Friday, as investors fled to safe havens. The 10-year Treasury yield dropped 10 basis points to 4.94%.

"Hopes that the Anthropic IPO would boost risk sentiment and trigger a recovery proved short lived," Kathleen Brooks, research director at trading platform XTB, said in a morning note. "European indices are under pressure this morning, and Asian indices are on track to experience their worst week since 2020."

Brooks added that "widespread risk aversion has gripped markets" as investors worry about "the leadership of Nvidia, the excessive spending to fund the AI build out and AI labs, rising interest rates, and the change of power to the Democrats in the US Congress."

Anthropic's IPO raised $81 billion, making it the largest on record. Shares opened 34% above their $83 offering price on Thursday but surrendered much of those gains, closing 17% higher.

Expectations of another Federal Reserve interest-rate hike added to pressure on richly valued technology stocks. Investors are increasingly looking for evidence that enormous spending on AI can generate sustainable profits, rather than simply fuel growth.

"This looks more like a valuation and financing reset than an immediate collapse in AI earnings," Charu Chanana, the chief investment strategist at Saxo, said in a note.

Wall Street's VIX, a gauge of expected stock-market volatility, jumped nearly 16% Thursday to close at 28.44.

Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone, warned that the selloff could feed on itself as rising volatility tightens risk limits, prompts investors to unwind leveraged positions, and adds selling pressure from systematic trading strategies.

"It’s difficult to envisage sustained upside in Anthropic without a broader recovery in risk appetite. For now, selling rallies appears the more compelling tactical approach, with the risk of further downside across both Anthropic and the wider AI complex," Weston wrote.

Red Friday: S&P 500 and the Dow hit correction territory, Nasdaq turns negative for the year

作者：Huileng Tan 您目前正在关注该作者！ Click to unsubscribe from email alerts. , Theron Mohamed You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts. ,and Jennifer Sor You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-20T19:04:57.804Z

The biggest IPO in history couldn't stop the bleeding in the broader market.

US tech shares fell sharply on Friday, with the Nasdaq Composite dropping nearly 3% to turn slightly negative for 2026. The S&P 500 was headed for a seventh-straight down day, on track for the worst losing streak since 2020. The benchmark index entered an official correction, down 10% from the October 6 peak, while the Dow also entered an official correction in late afternoon trading.

Here's where major indexes stood at 2 p.m. 和：

  • S&P 500: 7,027.22, down 2%
  • Dow Jones Industrial Average: 48,826.87, down 0.55% (-270 points)
  • Nasdaq 100: 25,515.80, down 3.8%

Anthropic stock fell 12% $85 a share after surging 17% in its debut on Thursday. Other tech heavyweights were also in the red, with SpaceX and Nvidia both down 6%, Meta falling 3%, and AMD stock down another 10% after its 8% fall on Thursday sparked by a short-seller's report about its exposure to China.

Nvidia's slide is particularly stark. The AI chip titan has lost 44% of its value since its October high of $243.37 as investors continue to flee the stock after Jensen Huang's departure and following its latest earnings.

Selling in stocks helped the bond market catch a bid on Friday, as investors fled to safe havens. The 10-year Treasury yield dropped 10 basis points to 4.94%.

"Hopes that the Anthropic IPO would boost risk sentiment and trigger a recovery proved short lived," Kathleen Brooks, research director at trading platform XTB, said in a morning note. "European indices are under pressure this morning, and Asian indices are on track to experience their worst week since 2020."

Brooks added that "widespread risk aversion has gripped markets" as investors worry about "the leadership of Nvidia, the excessive spending to fund the AI build out and AI labs, rising interest rates, and the change of power to the Democrats in the US Congress."

Anthropic's IPO raised $81 billion, making it the largest on record. Shares opened 34% above their $83 offering price on Thursday but surrendered much of those gains, closing 17% higher.

Expectations of another Federal Reserve interest-rate hike added to pressure on richly valued technology stocks. Investors are increasingly looking for evidence that enormous spending on AI can generate sustainable profits, rather than simply fuel growth.

"This looks more like a valuation and financing reset than an immediate collapse in AI earnings," Charu Chanana, the chief investment strategist at Saxo, said in a note.

Wall Street's VIX, a gauge of expected stock-market volatility, jumped nearly 16% Thursday to close at 28.44.

Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone, warned that the selloff could feed on itself as rising volatility tightens risk limits, prompts investors to unwind leveraged positions, and adds selling pressure from systematic trading strategies.

"It’s difficult to envisage sustained upside in Anthropic without a broader recovery in risk appetite. For now, selling rallies appears the more compelling tactical approach, with the risk of further downside across both Anthropic and the wider AI complex," Weston wrote.
